sections.title: Entangled logical qubits on a superconducting quantum processor
sections.abstract: The authors demonstrate logical surface-code operations, entanglement, and teleportation on a 120-qubit superconducting processor using lattice surgery, fast reset, and noise-informed decoding.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report logical Bell-state fidelities above 93%, teleportation fidelities of 78%–93%, and sub-1% logical error per round for distance-3 and distance-5 surface codes.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; 120 coupled superconducting qubits on IBM's ibm_phoenix processor, using surface codes and lattice surgery
sections.unique_caveat: Results rely on excluding underperforming components and noise-informed decoding on this particular device; they are not yet a demonstration of a scalable, general-purpose fault-tolerant computer.
sections.ranking_evidence: A direct hardware demonstration extends beyond logical memory to two-logical-qubit Bell-state entanglement and three-logical-qubit teleportation on a named processor, with quantitative fidelities reported.

sections.title: Three subpopulations of binary black holes in mass, spin magnitudes and tilts following GWTC-5
sections.abstract: Using 259 binary black holes in the fifth LIGO–Virgo–KAGRA catalog, the authors infer three mass-dependent subpopulations with distinct spin and mass-ratio distributions.
sections.claimed_result: The authors infer low-, medium-, and high-spin populations whose relative contributions vary with primary mass; the high-spin component dominates above roughly 60 solar masses.
sections.evidence_type: observational; hierarchical population inference from the LIGO–Virgo–KAGRA GWTC-5 catalog
sections.unique_caveat: Population structure and component assignments depend on the chosen mixture model; a fourth component does not resolve into a distinct distribution, and the inferred groups do not by themselves identify unique formation channels.
sections.ranking_evidence: The analysis uses the new 259-event GWTC-5 catalog, reports a three-component population result, and introduces variance control for resolving concentrated spin features.

sections.title: Comprehensive Visible and Near-infrared Keck and Gemini Monitoring and Characterization of Interstellar Comet 3I/ATLAS during its Encounter with the Solar System
sections.abstract: The authors report a multi-epoch optical and near-infrared observing record of interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS, tracing its dust activity, colours, gas ratios, and infrared spectrum from 2025 July to 2026 May.
sections.claimed_result: The authors find different inbound and outbound dust-activity trends and report no water-ice absorption robust to their tested continuum and calibration choices.
sections.evidence_type: observational; Keck/LRIS and MOSFIRE, Gemini/GMOS, Flamingos-2 and GNIRS observations
sections.unique_caveat: Dust-loss estimates assume grain sizes of 1 μm–1 mm and a nucleus model; the ice non-detection is conditional on the tested spectral-continuum and calibration treatments.
sections.ranking_evidence: An unusually broad Keck/Gemini time series combines optical imaging and spectroscopy with near-infrared imaging and spectroscopy; it also connects planetary and galactic astrophysics.
sections.comment: 53 pages, 21 figures, 9 tables. Submitted to AJ

sections.title: Galaxy Luminosity Functions at z~7-10 from Four Years of JWST Observations
sections.abstract: From four years of public JWST NIRCam imaging across nine fields, the authors estimate galaxy luminosity functions near redshifts 7.4 and 10, using NIRSpec confirmations to help quantify candidate contamination.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report a Schechter-like z≈7.4 luminosity function with faint-end slope −1.70±0.16, while the z≈10 sample is better fit by a power law with slope −2.36±0.16.
sections.evidence_type: observational; JWST public NIRCam imaging and NIRSpec spectroscopic redshifts, with statistical incompleteness and contamination corrections
sections.unique_caveat: The authors call for deeper imaging and spectroscopy near 30th magnitude to check the faint end and more bright-end spectroscopy (≲26th magnitude) to strengthen the z≈10 result.
sections.ranking_evidence: The analysis combines nine JWST fields spanning about 1,045 square arcminutes with thousands of dropout candidates and hundreds of secure NIRSpec redshifts; the preprint says it was submitted to MNRAS.

sections.title: The Galactic Center Gamma-Ray Excess and the Look-Elsewhere Effect
sections.abstract: Time-dependent cosmic-ray transport in simulated Milky Way analogues produces transient diffuse gamma-ray residuals that can resemble the spectrum and morphology of the Fermi-LAT Galactic Center Excess.
sections.claimed_result: The authors find simulated residuals several times larger than the Fermi excess in some snapshots and suggest that a transient stellar-source fluctuation could mimic it.
sections.evidence_type: computational; full magnetohydrodynamic simulations of Milky Way analogues with time-dependent cosmic-ray transport
sections.unique_caveat: This is a simulation-based interpretation, not a new Fermi-LAT detection or a demonstrated explanation of the excess; it depends on the simulated galaxy and cosmic-ray transport assumptions.
sections.ranking_evidence: The work links high-energy astrophysics, cosmology, and particle phenomenology, replacing steady-state and axisymmetric simplifications with time-dependent, spectrally resolved cosmic-ray transport in full-MHD galaxy simulations.

sections.title: Nano-ARPES observation of a flat band at the M point in 2.4° twisted bilayer graphene
sections.abstract: Nano-ARPES measurements reveal a flat band near the M point, away from the usual K-point focus, in a 2.4° twisted bilayer graphene sample.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report the first observation, in twisted bilayer graphene, of a flat band away from the K point, at M and far from the Fermi level.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; nano-focused angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (nano-ARPES) on 2.4° twisted bilayer graphene
sections.unique_caveat: The reported feature is from a particular twist angle and does not itself establish a superconducting or other correlated phase; replication across samples and angles is needed to assess its generality.
sections.ranking_evidence: A direct spectroscopic observation reports an unexpected band location and motivates measurements across the Brillouin zone; the paper cross-lists mesoscopic physics and materials science.
sections.comment: Main text (11 pages, 4 figures) and supplementary material (3 pages, 3 figures)
